critical_code_review_comments: server.py upload_document reads full file into memory before size check (data = await file.read()). For a truly huge upload this consumes RAM proportional to the request; acceptable given 10MB cap enforced at Nginx typically, but consider streaming with a running counter for defense-in-depth.
delete_parent_documents swallows all exceptions on fs_bucket.delete — fine for idempotency, but any real deletion failure will silently leak GridFS chunks. Consider logging the exception.

download_document returns Content-Disposition 'inline; filename="..."' — filenames are user-supplied; a filename containing a double-quote could break the header. Consider quoting/escaping or using RFC 5987 filename* for safety.

ALLOWED_DOC_EXT check is by filename suffix only (no content-type sniffing / magic-byte check). Malicious user could upload an .exe renamed to .pdf. Given this is a personal vault and data is encrypted at rest, low risk — but worth noting.
fs_bucket = AsyncIOMotorGridFSBucket(db) is created at import time; fine for single-worker uvicorn but should be created inside app lifespan for multi-worker deployments.
No index on documents.parent_id + parent_type — list/cascade queries will full-scan as collection grows. Add compound index in startup create_indexes().
